clocks.label: FOMC DECISION
clocks.why: The meeting behind GEO-029 at 63 per cent. Three members already dissented FOR a hike in July while PCE runs 3.7 per cent, and Brent is now at $99. This is the clock that decides whether the world's reserve central bank tightens INTO an oil supply shock - the configuration that historically breaks levered positions elsewhere.

clocks.label: BOJ DECISION
clocks.why: Two days after the Fed, and the clock behind GEO-025 at 29 per cent. The carry unwind needs both legs; a Tokyo hike into a hawkish Fed is the 2024 August template. HELD today only because no fresh yen print was established, not because the setup weakened.

clocks.label: BERLIN + MV VOTE
clocks.why: Two more Land elections thirteen days after Saxony-Anhalt, and the first test of whether 43.9 per cent was Land-specific or a national repricing. Prices GEO-028 at 23 and the SAXONY-ANHALT THIRD BALLOT wire. Note the variable being tested: anti-AfD street mobilisation is exactly what failed on 6 September.

clocks.label: HORMUZ FALSIFIER
clocks.why: Our own dated falsifier, published in advance so it can be scored against us, with two legs. Leg one: an attack on a laden tanker inside the INTERNATIONAL LANES. Leg two: Iran publishing coordinates for its restricted zone, or an Omani co-signature. Neither has landed, and non-occurrence scores against the escalation model.

clocks.label: BRENT BARRIER
clocks.why: GEO-009 resolves on a daily CLOSE and Brent sits eight-tenths of one per cent under the $100 wall with eleven sessions to run. Cut to 17 per cent today on a recomputed discrete-monitoring barrier. This delivers this board its FIRST Brier score after 31 open questions and zero resolutions.

clocks.label: XI STATE VISIT
clocks.why: The visit GEO-006 rides at 90 per cent and GEO-012 at 31. Now carrying a numbered deliverable - reciprocal tariff cuts on $30bn of goods each way - which is what turned GEO-007 down to 18. The same day Brent's band question resolves, so this board gets its summit and its first score in one session.

speculation.obs: A think-tank imagery team published a physical assessment of Iran's most protected site days before the president threatened it, and the assessment is more careful than the threat. As published by CSIS, reading Airbus very-high-resolution imagery from 9 July 2026 and Satellogic imagery from 9 August against six years of synthetic aperture radar, there is more road activity at Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La in 2026 than at any point in the site's history, with heavy simultaneous usage across every road corridor since January; the south and east tunnel portals are visibly more hardened than in September 2025, concrete surfacing has been added over roads and external portal accesses, and Iran completed the security perimeter fence around the entire facility between June and September 2025. The authors state explicitly that their assessment 'can neither refute nor substantiate' the Israeli claim that centrifuges were moved inside.
speculation.src: CSIS, Satellite Imagery Analysis of Pickaxe Mountain
speculation.read: Labelled inference. The most load-bearing sentence in the study is the negative one, and it is the sentence the political use of this imagery drops: continuous construction combined with the ABSENCE of a heightened internal security posture suggests the site is not yet capable of enrichment work. Read that way, the imagery describes a building site rather than a facility, which is a very different object to threaten - and it means the observation currently supports a bargaining threat better than it supports a target. It also means the analysts and the podium are looking at the same pixels and saying different things, which is the gap worth watching.
speculation.falsifier: Imagery showing a heightened internal security posture, hardened checkpoints or the personnel and vehicle signature of an operating facility - or an IAEA statement that enrichment has begun there - confirms the site has crossed from construction to capability and makes it a real target. Continued portal and road work with no change in internal security, through October, keeps this in the announcement column.

speculation.obs: An open-source geolocation account placed Houthi forces inside Mocha with a coordinate before the wires had confirmed the city had fallen. As published by GeoConfirmed, footage of a Houthi technical entering Main Street in Mocha in front of the Taizi Mall was geolocated to 13.3216146, 43.2567378, timed to around noon local Yemen time, with local chanting audible on the clip.
speculation.src: GeoConfirmed, circulated on X and reposted to imageboards
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and the inference is about the reporting layer rather than the war. A single geolocated coordinate settled a question that competing official statements could not - the government side was still describing a repositioning while the coordinate showed a technical on the main street. That is the routine now: the geolocation arrives first and the wire copy catches up, which means the same technique is the fastest available check on the claims moving ahead of the wires today, specifically the assertion that Zuqar island and the entire chokepoint coastline have already fallen.
speculation.falsifier: A geolocated image or verified satellite pass placing Houthi forces on Zuqar or the Hanish islands confirms the wider claim now circulating. Absence of any geolocation for the islands within 72 hours, while Mocha itself is repeatedly confirmed, means the coastline claim has outrun the evidence.

speculation.obs: A commercial maritime-intelligence desk has published a hull-count baseline at Bab el-Mandeb that was taken BEFORE Mocha fell, which turns the next two weekly counts into a measurement rather than an argument. As published by Lloyd's List Intelligence's Maritime Intelligence Unit, 302 passings were recorded in the week to 23 August of which 257 were AIS-traceable, 202 traceable transits followed in the week to 30 August, and the average for 27 July to 23 August was 273 ships a week against a pre-blockade norm of 319. The same brief states the industry's working assumption in plain words: that Houthi threats are limited to a specific subset of Saudi-linked tonnage rather than a broad threat to the wider trade.
speculation.src: Lloyd's List Intelligence, Red Sea Brief, 3 September 2026
speculation.read: Labelled inference, carried forward and now more load-bearing than when it was written. If the reading is right, the strait has stayed open on a BELIEF rather than on a balance of force - owners kept transiting because they judged the threat addressed to Riyadh rather than to them. A belief reprices in an afternoon in a way a minefield does not, and the arrival of Iranian officers and Iranian resupply on the Yemeni coast is exactly the kind of fact that makes an underwriter reconsider who the threat is addressed to. War-risk at Bab el-Mandeb currently sits around 0.5 per cent of hull value.
speculation.falsifier: Weekly Bab el-Mandeb transits holding near 270 through end-September confirms Mocha bought position rather than closure. A fall below roughly 150, or a war-risk quotation that stops distinguishing Saudi-linked tonnage from the general trade, kills the reading and means the belief has broken.

dossiers.name: Iran

glance.government: Islamic Republic - a clerical-military hybrid in which the security institutions have been ascendant since the February-May war
glance.leader: Mojtaba Khamenei, Supreme Leader since 8 Mar 2026, not verifiably seen in public for roughly six months; Masoud Pezeshkian president; IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi the operative center
glance.gdp: Roughly $300-390bn nominal depending on source; forecast to contract about 5% in 2026 with inflation near 70% and the rial at a record 2.02m to the dollar
glance.military: About 570,000-610,000 active (IISS puts it near 570,000) plus roughly 350,000 reserves; the IRGC Navy, not the regular navy, holds the strait
glance.influence: Transit rights and mine inventory at Hormuz, anti-ship missiles, Iraqi and Yemeni networks - set against oil revenue the central bank governor himself describes as having fallen to zero

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint, not the man. Iran is a state whose one convertible asset - the barrel - has stopped moving, which is why its remaining leverage is geographic rather than economic, and why it is spent in advertised doses rather than banked. The desk that decides is the IRGC Navy and the new wartime security committee, not the presidency and not the invisible Leader: Washington routed its own peace offer through career Guard commanders, and Iran's president has said on state television that communicating with Khamenei is very difficult. That produces exactly the behaviour this board keeps recording - a volley at forewarned bases in Jordan that was almost entirely intercepted, mines laid and lanes conditionally cleared, six near-breakthroughs that each end in a restated condition. Prospect theory says a cornered regime gambles, but a regime whose survival runs through an institution that profits from the crisis has an interest in holding the temperature where it can still choose it. The falsifier is a strike that actually kills Americans, or a verified minesweeping calendar with published coordinates - either would show the temperature is no longer being chosen.

concerns: Mine and anti-ship capability at Hormuz is intact and reversible - a cleared lane is a maintenance schedule, not a settlement
Succession is unresolved in practice: an unseen Leader plus an IRGC that answers Washington's messages is a leadership fiction with a real chain of command underneath
Oil revenue near zero against 70% inflation removes the economic off-ramp that would normally price restraint
Escalation is now probabilistic rather than intentional - interception rates, not decisions, separate a message from a casualty event

Retaliation has gone HORIZONTAL: fire into US facilities in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait in a single night widens the number of surfaces on which the interception equilibrium can fail, and converts Gulf hosts from venues into potential parties

The war has reached the LOADING POINT: Iranian state media says four US missiles hit a tanker six miles off Kharg on 5 September, and Iran fired anti-ship and ballistic missiles toward the strait the day before. Unconfirmed, and the terminals themselves are still unstruck - but the one asset with any convertible value left is now inside the target set

dossiers.name: Russia

glance.government: Presidential autocracy with a managed legislature; State Duma elections due September 2026
glance.leader: Vladimir Putin - the only decider on the war file; Peskov is a thermostat, not an actor
glance.population: About 144 million (2026 estimate; occupied-territory counting disputed)
glance.gdp: Roughly $2.7tn nominal; the government cut its 2026 growth forecast toward 0.4-1%, with oil and gas revenue reported down more than 25%
glance.military: About 1.3 million active with roughly 2 million reserves; defence spending near 6.3-6.5% of GDP
glance.influence: Sanctioned-barrel logistics including the Arctic route, Africa Corps guarantees in the Sahel, energy leverage over Europe, veto and nuclear status

dossiers.summary: Moscow's constraint is refining and money, not morale. Ukrainian deep strikes have pushed refinery runs to about 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since 2002, and the fuel export ban first imposed in July is being weighed for a second extension - each extension a public admission of how much capacity is offline. The deciding desks are the defence and finance ministries rather than the foreign ministry: the September Duma election and the 6.3-6.5% of GDP the war costs are what price the negotiating posture, which is why the deep pause Peskov announced reads as a bargaining position taken from a front that is still moving at Pokrovsk. Watch where the state chose to spend a scarce asset this weekend - Africa Corps, roughly 200-300 personnel supplied overland through Burkina Faso, was used to save a junta in Niamey, buying an advertisement and incurring an obligation in the same act. The observables that would move this file are not statements but airlift and diesel: Flight Unit 224 traffic above its six-flight run rate, or refinery runs recovering past 4m barrels a day.

concerns: The fuel and refining constraint is the real bind - denial is working where punishment has not, and Kyiv is aiming at exactly that
The announced campaign against Ukraine's grid is punishment by Pape's definition, with a poor historical conversion into concessions
Sahel guarantees now carry a defend-the-palace obligation a 200-300 person detachment cannot scale
September Duma elections and a possible post-election reserve call-up are the domestic clock every diplomatic signal is priced against

The covert front against the supplier coalition is now formally attributed: Berlin blames Moscow for an explosive drone at Leipzig/Halle and closes the Bonn consulate on Sept 18, with the EU calling it state-sponsored terrorism - salami tactics against logistics rather than against forces

First reciprocated pause of the war, and it is a bargaining instrument rather than fatigue: Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for 72 hours from midnight on 5 September, explicitly tied to the American envoys' visit, hours after striking Ukrainian airports and infrastructure and with Ryabkov restating that Washington must accept realities on the ground

dossiers.name: Ukraine

glance.government: Wartime presidential republic under martial law; national elections suspended for the duration
glance.leader: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, constrained by coalition dependence; Rustem Umerov holds both the negotiating brief and the intelligence file
glance.population: About 39.5 million on mid-2026 estimates - wartime displacement makes every figure soft
glance.gdp: Roughly $225bn nominal (2025); the EU agreed a package of about EUR 90bn for 2026-27, funded by market borrowing rather than by seizing the roughly EUR 210bn of frozen Russian assets
glance.military: About 677,000 active on the IISS count; larger figures circulate and are not verified
glance.influence: A deep-strike drone campaign that has taken Russian refining to a 24-year low, the Black Sea corridor, and the political weight of being the coalition's test case

dossiers.summary: Kyiv's constraint is arithmetic - manpower, interceptors and a donor calendar - and it sets the strategy rather than following from it. The one instrument Ukraine owns outright is the drone campaign against Russian refineries, which is denial in Pape's sense and is measurably working; nearly everything else is rented from capitals that vote. That dependence is why the deciding desk is now split between the general staff and a negotiating channel run through Washington, and why Zelenskyy has to say yes to the joint Western plan and no to surrender in the same breath. It also explains Myla: an army under sustained deep strike disperses munitions into settlements, which lowers the odds of losing a depot and raises the odds of a night like Friday's, when 38 people died mostly from what the warehouse contained. The falsifiable claim for the winter is that Russia's fuel constraint shapes Russian behaviour more than blackouts shape Ukrainian negotiating positions - if Kyiv's position visibly softens under grid attack while Moscow's does not under fuel shortage, the model is wrong and we say so.

concerns: The announced Russian campaign against the electricity grid arrives with winter and with air-defence stocks already rationed
Pokrovsk is the axis Moscow names when it explains why it is in no hurry to talk; its fall would be a step change, not a line move
Funding is market-borrowed rather than asset-backed, which puts the money on a European political calendar
Dispersal of munitions into inhabited areas makes mass-casualty events recurrent regardless of anyone's aimpoint

dossiers.name: China

glance.government: Party-state under the most centralized leadership since Mao; a recent command purge reshaped the military timetable
glance.leader: Xi Jinping; Wang Yi carries the foreign file with delegated authority
glance.gdp: About $20.9tn nominal (IMF, 2026); 4.7% growth in the first half against a 4.5-5% target, July exports up 23.9% year on year
glance.military: About 2.0 million active, the largest standing force in the world; announced defence budget in the $280bn range
glance.influence: Buyer of last resort for sanctioned barrels, rare earths and the export machine, coast-guard jurisdiction pressure around Taiwan and the East China Sea, and a summit Washington wants

dossiers.summary: Beijing's constraint this quarter is the calendar, not the doctrine. A state visit on 24 September and a tariff truce expiring in November are both worth more than any concession on Iranian crude, which is why the buying continues while the rhetoric stays defiant - and why Treasury sanctioned an Egyptian bank's UAE branches rather than a Chinese one. An enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is telling you which nail is expensive. The desk to watch is not the foreign ministry but the coast guard and the customs administration: PLA sorties around Taiwan have been declining while jurisdictional assertion has been rising, and that ratchet - salami tactics in Schelling's sense, slices too thin to fight over individually - is the actual instrument. Read the summit as accumulation under cover of detente rather than as a thaw, and keep the discount small: announced head-of-state visits with active staff preparation happen about 90% of the time. The tell that breaks the benign read is a coast-guard action inside the visit window; the tell that breaks the leverage read is a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before 24 September.

concerns: Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building around Taiwan, not the event itself
China is the load-bearing leak in the Iran sanctions siege - Mulder's rule is that a siege is only as tight as its leakage path
The tariff truce expires in November, just after the summit, which is where a cheap concession becomes an expensive one
A defiant public line paired with quiet compliance makes intent unreadable from statements; only flows settle it

dossiers.name: Israel

glance.government: Parliamentary democracy; the Knesset dissolved in July and the election is set for 27 October 2026
glance.leader: Benjamin Netanyahu, prime minister; Israel Katz defence minister and the cabinet's designated hawk
glance.gdp: About $720bn nominal on 2026 estimates, with defence spending near 8% of GDP
glance.influence: Air superiority over the Levant, the Washington relationship, and an undeclared nuclear status the state has never confirmed

dossiers.summary: Read every Israeli decision for the next seven weeks through 27 October. That is the constraint, and it is a calendar rather than a character: a prime minister facing an election needs deliverables that are visible, mapped and finished, which is exactly what a declared security zone is. On 4 September Katz said the capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge completes the phase of securing control in southern Lebanon and that there will be no withdrawal until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout the country - a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to meet, which makes the presence open-ended by construction. The desk that decides is not the cabinet podium but Northern Command's force-generation math and the finance ministry's reserve-duty bill, because holding ground costs manpower in a way air power does not. Note also the direction this cuts: history says a held buffer produces chronic attrition rather than episodic campaigns, which is why this board CUT its multi-week-campaign odds on the day the zone was declared. Separately, national security minister Ben Gvir published a twenty-page plan for what he calls voluntary emigration of Gaza's population - 250,000 in the first year and the remainder over six more. It is a minister's document rather than cabinet policy, and forced transfer of civilians from occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions; it is logged here as a coalition signal, not as a programme.

concerns: The 27 October election makes restraint politically expensive at exactly the wrong moment
A withdrawal condition the Lebanese state cannot satisfy converts an operation into an occupation by definition
The Lebanon framework still has no third-party verifier and the party being disarmed rejects the premise
Ministerial transfer plans for Gaza, even unimplemented, carry legal and coalition exposure that outlasts the cabinet

dossiers.name: Germany

glance.government: Federal parliamentary republic; sixteen Laender, each electing its own Minister-President. Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote 20 September 2026
glance.leader: Friedrich Merz, chancellor, whose CDU just lost 25 of its 40 seats in Saxony-Anhalt; Ulrich Siegmund leads the AfD there and has said he will not stand for Minister-President without a stable majority
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.9tn nominal - unverified against a current print; Jaguar Land Rover cutting 4,000 jobs and Volkswagen repurposing a plant for defence are the texture of the industrial quarter
glance.military: About 182,000 active on standard counts, with rearmament running against recruitment shortfalls; unverified against a current IISS figure
glance.influence: Europe's largest industrial gas consumer, the logistics bridge to Ukraine through Leipzig/Halle, and the swing vote on every EU sanctions and energy instrument

dossiers.summary: Germany's constraint stopped being abstract on Sunday. The AfD took 43.9 per cent and 39 of 83 seats in Saxony-Anhalt on turnout that rose from about 60 to about 80 per cent, and the CDU fell to 17.2 per cent - which means the late-mobilisation argument that has contained the AfD in every previous Land election did not work, and ING said so in as many words. The desk that now decides is not the federal party presidium in Berlin, which can only expel people; it is the Landtag running ballots in Magdeburg, where a third round for Minister-President is settled by a simple majority of votes cast and the five-seat BSW can decide the outcome by abstaining. Underneath the politics the older vice is unchanged: Germany replaced Russian pipeline gas with seaborne LNG, trading a political dependency for a maritime one, so a war at Hormuz reaches German industry directly - and it remains the physical bridge over which munitions reach Ukraine, which is why a drone came down at Leipzig/Halle rather than at a barracks. Two more elections land on 20 September.

concerns: A Land where no majority exists without breaking one of two taboos - the CDU has excluded both the AfD and Die Linke, and the third-ballot rule rewards deadlock
Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote on 20 September, thirteen days after the mobilisation defence visibly failed
Fraud narratives spread within hours of the count, part of them traced by DW's fact-check desk to the Matryoshka influence operation - contested results are now a standing feature of German elections
A sabotage campaign aimed at logistics rather than forces sits deliberately below any alliance threshold, and Lavrov has answered Berlin's attribution by calling it the start of a real war
Energy input cost remains the binding industrial number, and seaborne LNG means Hormuz is now a German domestic-politics variable

dossiers.name: United States

glance.government: Federal presidential republic; midterm elections 3 November 2026
glance.leader: Donald Trump; Scott Bessent at Treasury, Marco Rubio at State, Pete Hegseth at Defense, Kevin Warsh at the Federal Reserve
glance.gdp: Roughly $30tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; federal debt past $40tn
glance.military: About 1.34 million active with roughly 770,000 reserve and National Guard; budget in the $900bn range
glance.influence: Dollar clearing and OFAC designations, CENTCOM escort of the strait, and a rate path that prices everyone else's oil bill

dossiers.summary: The American constraint hardened today and it is arithmetic rather than politics. August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1%, which removes the soft-landing argument for cutting; simultaneously diesel set an all-time record at $5.820 a gallon on a refining shortage no interest rate can fix. That is the RESCUE WITHHELD configuration - a market pricing help in a shock where help does not exist - and the long end already agrees, with the ten-year at 4.79% and the thirty-year at 5.27%, both above this board's published red lines, and the reverse-repo buffer down to $0.70bn. The desk that decides is not the podium: it is the FOMC, the refiners' turnaround calendar and the weekly EIA distillate print, in that order of who can actually change the number. Foreign policy is being run on the same logic - allies invoiced for contributions at Hormuz, a Venezuelan venture organised around one man's legal exposure rather than around built infrastructure, and a president who declined this week to say whether the United States would defend Britain in another Falklands war. Each of those is leverage bought cheaply now against a commitment payable later.

concerns: Record diesel is the invisible half of the inflation problem, because it prices freight, farming and heating rather than only the pump
A hot labour print into a hiking debate removes the monetary rescue markets keep assuming
Enforcement at Hormuz is now a standing commitment - a lane you must keep clearing is not a victory
Alliance ambiguity is being used as leverage in three theatres at once, and credibility spent in one is not recoverable in another
Confirmed American casualties would collapse the intercepted-volley equilibrium the whole restraint posture rests on

dossiers.name: Japan

glance.government: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system; Bank of Japan policy decision due 18 September 2026
glance.leader: Emperor Naruhito as head of state; the offices that matter for this file are the Bank of Japan policy board and the Ministry of Finance FX desk - not the cabinet
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.2tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; policy rate 0.75 per cent, a thirty-year high, with ten-year government bond yields near 3 per cent for the first time since 1996
glance.military: Self-Defense Forces of about 247,000 active personnel; defence spending on a path toward 2 per cent of GDP
glance.influence: The world's cheap funding currency, one of the largest foreign holders of US Treasuries, and a carry trade estimated anywhere between $500bn and over $4tn depending on definition

dossiers.summary: Japan's constraint became visible in a number this week: 15.4 trillion yen, about $98.6bn, spent in a single month defending the currency, and reporting that it likely sold US Treasuries to fund it. For thirty years Japan supplied the world with money that cost nothing and the world spent it on everything from Mexican bonds to American technology; that arrangement is unwinding because Japan finally has inflation, imported partly through a weak yen and partly through an energy bill that this year's Hormuz disruption made worse. The desk that decides is the BoJ policy board on 18 September, and the yen has already run to 154.06 on the expectation. What is genuinely new is the American side of the plumbing: Washington joined the July intervention and Bessent pushed the Fed to widen the FIMA repo facility, which lets Tokyo borrow dollars against its Treasuries instead of selling them. Read that as the balance-of-financial-terror being actively managed - the US needs its largest foreign creditor not to become a seller during a heavy issuance calendar, and it built a valve to make sure.

concerns: A disorderly carry unwind transmits a Tokyo rate decision into global asset prices within hours, as it did in August 2024
The size of the borrowed-yen stack is genuinely unknown - published estimates span an order of magnitude
A currency defence funded by Treasury sales raises US long-end yields at the exact moment the ten-year sits above 4.75 per cent
A defence financed by repo must be repeatedly refinanced, which converts a one-off intervention into a standing obligation
Imported energy costs are the transmission line from the Strait of Hormuz into Japanese inflation and therefore into this policy decision

scenarios.q: What if the Houthis hit a Saudi crude EXPORT terminal rather than a refinery?
scenarios.read: Everything so far has landed on refining, utilities and an airbase - assets that cost Riyadh money and cost the world diesel. Ras Tanura and Yanbu are a different category: together they load the overwhelming majority of Saudi crude exports, and Ras Tanura alone is the largest offshore loading facility on earth. Hitting one converts a price story into a volume story, and it is the point at which Washington's calculus stops resembling Abqaiq - because Abqaiq was repaired in weeks while a damaged sea-island loading berth is a shipping-schedule problem measured in months.

stages.s: A - continued strikes on refining, utilities and airbases; Brent stays in the high nineties on a war premium that decays
B - a strike on export infrastructure with loadings interrupted for under a week; Brent breaches $100 on closes and GEO-009 resolves NO
C - sustained export interruption forcing an IEA coordinated release or a US SPR draw
D - direct US kinetic response against Iranian territory attributed to the terminal strike

scenarios.falsifier: Saudi crude loadings at Ras Tanura and Yanbu holding at recent volumes through 30 September. If they hold while strikes continue, stage A is the correct model and stages C and D should be cut.

scenarios.q: What if Brent closes above $100 before 24 September?
scenarios.read: This is not a speculative branch, it is a live barrier eight-tenths of one per cent away with eleven sessions on the clock, and it is the first thing on this board that will actually be SCORED. The mechanism to watch is not the headline but the term structure: a spot spike on an outage flattens or backwardates the curve, while a spike that drags December 2027 up with it is the market repricing the war as structural. Goldman already moved multi-year shipping disruption from its risk case into its base case last week, which is the analytical version of the same move.

stages.s: A - Brent closes above $100 at least once; GEO-009 resolves NO and this board takes a Brier score on a 17 per cent mark
B - the far end of the curve rises with spot, indicating a structural rather than an outage repricing
C - a coordinated IEA or SPR release announced in response
D - demand destruction visible in refinery runs or product demand within the window

scenarios.falsifier: Brent closing below $95 for five consecutive sessions before 24 September. That would say the geometry overweighted realised volatility and the drift term was wrong, and the anchor should be rebuilt upward.

scenarios.q: What if the Xi summit produces the $30bn reciprocal tariff cut?
scenarios.read: The tell would not be the number, it would be the instrument. A joint statement is reversible in a morning; a published Federal Register notice amending the tariff schedule is administrative and sticky, because unwinding it requires the same process that built it. That distinction is the whole difference between a photograph and a transaction, and it is why this board watches USTR's exclusion process rather than the podium.

stages.s: A - the summit happens and produces a communique with the $30bn figure but no instrument
B - a published tariff-schedule amendment or Federal Register notice within 30 days
C - the November truce expiry passes with an extension rather than a renegotiation
D - the 7.5 per cent overcapacity finding is published anyway, and the cut coexists with an escalation on a separate file

scenarios.falsifier: Publication of the overcapacity finding or a top-ten Chinese bank designation before 24 September. Either would say the summit is a venue for delivering bad news rather than a deal, and GEO-007 deserves a raise rather than the cut taken today.

chatter.claim: That the newly released 9/11 files prove the government knew the air at Ground Zero was poisonous and told people it was safe anyway - and that if they lied about that, the standing questions about the day itself are back open. The release is being read on the boards as a partial, curated drop timed for the 25th anniversary, with the harder claim that the genuinely damaging material is in the boxes still being reviewed.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread titled around the declassification drew 59 replies and fed several anniversary threads, including a long-running 'you're trapped in the North Tower, can you escape' engineering thread at 105 replies and a 'this is why they chose 9/11' numerology thread; it is circulating alongside heavy X and Reddit traffic on the anniversary.
chatter.read: The kernel here is not a theory, it is documented: Mayor Mamdani's administration opened a public portal on 8 September with roughly 170,000 pages including the Harding Memo, 68 boxes found in 2025 and Giuliani-era records, settling two 9/11 Health Watch lawsuits, and the records do show officials aware of asbestos concerns while publicly reassuring New Yorkers. The 'so the rest is open too' step is the leap - a proven institutional lie about air quality is evidence about bureaucratic incentive under litigation exposure, not about the physics of the day. The timing complaint is answerable: the city said further tranches will be released over the coming year with identifying information removed.

chatter.claim: That the Pickaxe Mountain threat is theatre because the target is physically un-hittable - 'there is no weapon on earth that can crack over 100 metres of granite' - and the real tell is Trump saying the war will not end until after the election, which prompted the direct question 'how does he know?'. The circulating conclusion is that the strike, if it comes, will be scheduled by the American electoral calendar rather than by anything happening inside the mountain.
chatter.spread: /pol/'s Persia-Israel general, edition 2,095, past 300 replies, with the midterm-timing exchange spawning a long sub-thread and an Israeli Channel 13 'movement detected' report circulating as the pre-placed trigger.
chatter.read: This is the wag-the-dog frame and it has an unusually strong factual base for a board theory: the schedule claim is Trump's own words, and CSIS puts the chambers at least 100 metres down behind U-bend portals specifically shaped to defeat penetrators. Where it overreaches is the inference from un-strikeable to staged. A threat you cannot execute is still a cheap instrument for pricing a negotiation, and the oil tape moved within the hour, which is the boring explanation doing all the work.

chatter.claim: That Saudi Arabia is structurally collapsing rather than merely losing a Yemeni front - 'expect them to lose Aden too' - and that the collapse is being concealed. Alongside it runs the claim that the Houthi advance is impossible on its own terms, that sandal-wearing irregulars cannot beat air superiority, and that the only explanation is either Iranian officers running the operation or a quiet Gulf handover of the coast in exchange for calling off strikes on Saudi energy facilities.
chatter.spread: Several concurrent /pol/ threads - a gloating Saudi-collapse thread at 171 replies, the coastline seizure thread at 142, a 'how is this technically possible' thread, plus a breaking post claiming Zuqar island has already fallen, attributed to wire sourcing the wires have not published.
chatter.read: This is the sold-out-by-your-patron frame applied to Kabul 2021 and Syrian army units in 2024, and one leg of it is genuinely on the wires rather than fringe: France 24 reports IRGC guidance to the coastal advance and Iranian promises of more weapons and senior officers. The Gulf-consent leg is the weak one, since Saudi aircraft flew strikes on Houthi positions the day before Mocha fell. The Zuqar claim should be treated as unconfirmed - Mocha has been geolocated, the islands have not.

A second strand calls it a deliberate $1.5 trillion detonation of the dollar, and a third stacks DOGE savings, tariff checks and the dividend into a claimed $12,000 per citizen.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread at 82 replies plus several smaller vote-buying threads, a /biz/ thread at 54 running US10Y and US30Y implications off a viral Kobeissi Letter post, and a widely shared 'what is the angle here, genuinely?' thread at 56.
chatter.read: The first strand is a coalition read rather than a conspiracy theory, and it is checkable: an offer that grows as the legal lever fails is evidence about the offeror's own estimate of the race, and bill text before November settles it. The inflation arithmetic in the second strand is loose - the 2020-21 checks were roughly $814 billion inside a much larger package - but the instinct about a trillion-dollar transfer meeting a 5.30 per cent thirty-year during an energy shock is not wrong.

chatter.claim: That oil is not spiking on war risk at all but on physical exhaustion - 'the delulu market is just slowly coming to terms that oil is running out', $150 by year end - and that the record diesel print is the proof, because distillate is the one product a reserve release cannot fake. Running beside it: an 'EXIT ALL MARKETS NOW, buy guns, ammo, gold, silver, canned food' thread, and the claim that the rate path is an engineered squeeze on households under cover of the war.
chatter.spread: Diesel-record threads running simultaneously on /pol/ (60 replies) and /biz/ (90 and climbing), four concurrent Stock Market Generals including 'Oil barons and bobos edition' and 'The Final Boss Edition', a Cramer clip repackaged as '$150 is about to be reality', and a Monero and precious-metals general both busier than usual.
chatter.read: Peak-oil is the frame; the usable kernel is narrower. Distillate really is the tight link - refineries cannot switch product mix quickly, the SPR holds crude not diesel, and a 24.1 per cent monthly move in the fuel that moves freight is physical. What the claim cannot carry is 'running out': OPEC+ removed its capping mechanism this year, so the constraint is where spare barrels SIT, behind two contested straits.

chatter.claim: That the emergency broadcast infrastructure is being quietly rehearsed for war - 'BREAKING! They are testing the WW3 alarms right now!' - with posters comparing siren and alert tests across regions and reading the coincidence with the Hormuz tanker exchange as deliberate conditioning rather than routine scheduling.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread at 120 replies, cross-posted into the Iran generals and echoed on X, sitting alongside a 190-reply 'the US is fucking cooked' thread.
chatter.read: This is the standard alert-test-as-omen frame, which recurs on every scheduled EAS and siren test and has a 100 per cent false-positive record so far. The kernel that is real is not the sirens but the mood: alert-test threads spike when a population is already primed, so their volume is a decent sentiment gauge even when the claim is empty. Worth reading as a thermometer, not as intelligence.

chatter.claim: That King Felipe VI of Spain is preparing the military to remove the civilian government 'to save the people', circulated off a single X video post and picked up as a coming European domino.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread at 96 replies built entirely around the one X link; it runs alongside a 221-reply thread on Orban, Meloni and Le Pen publicly criticising the AfD as too radical over its remigration plans, and a Kraut/pol/ general.
chatter.read: Single-source and unverified, and it fits a recognisable species: the monarch-as-saviour narrative that recurs wherever a European right feels blocked by its own coalition partners. The checkable kernel is the AfD story next to it, which is the real one - established nationalist leaders distancing themselves from a more radical partner is a coalition event with consequences, and it is being emotionally processed through a coup fantasy about a different country.

chatter.claim: That the Covid vaccines are a cancer-inducing bioweapon and that a newly posted case report is the hard evidence, with a Zenodo record circulated as the citation; a companion memory-holed thread on /x/ collects older items including claims of Bluetooth signals emitted from vaccinated graves.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread at 149 replies pushing the Zenodo record, and an /x/ 'things that were memory-holed' thread at 283 replies carrying the older material.
chatter.read: The persuasion technique to name is citation-laundering: a Zenodo record is a self-deposit archive with no peer review, so the link supplies the visual grammar of a citation without the filter, and the thread's authority comes entirely from that formatting. The checkable kernel that keeps this narrative alive is real institutional behaviour - myocarditis signals were downplayed before they were acknowledged - which is why the frame keeps finding recruits and why it will not be argued down with a link.

chatter.claim: That NATO's Article 5 would be invoked, or conspicuously not invoked, if China moved on Taiwan, with the circulating conclusion that European members would refuse and the alliance would be exposed as a paper guarantee - 'and then everyone says fuck off'.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread at 151 replies, amplified by NATO Secretary General Rutte's comment on the wires that the alliance will stay 'strong' whoever wins the French election.
chatter.read: The claim rests on a category error worth naming, because it is doing real work in how people read the alliance: Article 5 covers the North Atlantic area and would not apply to Taiwan at all, so the scenario cannot happen as described. The kernel underneath is a genuine question that serious planners share - whether a simultaneous Pacific and European demand would find the alliance able to answer either - and it is sharpened by a French election in which the NATO commitment is itself contested.

chatter.claim: That 2027 is the convergence year - a date arrived at independently by unrelated esoteric sources, astrological, substack-prophetic and numerological, and now being cross-referenced against the war calendar and the debt-rollover calendar as though the three were the same clock.
chatter.spread: An /x/ thread at 71 replies with substack and video sources, feeding a much larger board mood: a 1,396-reply Nobody General, a 361-reply divination general, and repeated 'tell me it's going to be ok' threads.
chatter.read: Date-convergence claims are a self-fulfilling genre - once a year is named, later sources cite the earlier ones and the independence that made it impressive evaporates. It is included because the pattern is worth tracking rather than the prophecy: apocalyptic date-setting volume rises with material stress, and this board is currently running it at unusual intensity alongside a record diesel print and two contested straits.

chatter.claim: That Ukraine's war reporting on both sides is now essentially fabricated, with the Russia-aligned general warning readers that any thread citing Ukrainian sources is 'video game footage' and the Ukraine-aligned general running casualty totals the other side calls invented; both are circulating today around the report that Zelensky's aircraft was nearly struck by a drone en route to Oslo.
chatter.spread: Two parallel /pol/ generals - the Russia-aligned one at 242 replies on edition 24,078, the Ukraine-aligned one at 139 on edition 20,129 - plus a 104-reply thread accusing the board of being astroturfed by both governments.
chatter.read: This is the mirror-image epistemic collapse that makes a theater hard to read, and it is data in itself: when both camps pre-emptively define the other's evidence as fake, no new fact can settle anything and the belief distribution freezes. The checkable item under it is the Norwegian prime minister's own statement about the drone near-miss, which is an official source outside both camps - the kind of fact that briefly moves people, and the reason officials from third countries are increasingly the only usable witnesses in this war.

easy.bottomLine: The American president warned Iran about a nuclear site buried so deep inside a mountain that no bomb can reach it, and said the war will not end until after November's elections. In Yemen, fighters kept pushing along the coast toward one of the world's narrowest shipping doors, with help from Iran. Oil went past $105 a barrel and truck fuel hit a record price, so America's central bank is now likely to raise interest rates next week. And the Supreme Court stopped Missouri from using a new voting map that would have helped Republicans win an extra seat.
easy.risk: Still HIGH, not raised. This board only goes to its top level if an American is killed or an American ship is hit. Neither happened today, even though three separate dangerous things did: Iran and America attacked each other's ships, the fighters in Yemen took more coastline, and the president named Iran's most protected nuclear site as a target. More danger in more places, but the line that matters was not crossed.
easy.markets: Oil is at about $105 a barrel and American truck fuel is at a record $5.98 a gallon after jumping 24 per cent in one month. Diesel matters more than petrol because trucks, trains and tractors run on it, so when it jumps, food and delivery prices follow a few months later. Wholesale prices are up 5.4 per cent over the year, and traders now think there is about a 70 per cent chance America raises interest rates next Wednesday. Europe already raised its rate this morning.
brief: Iran built a secret complex inside a mountain near its main nuclear plant, dug so deep under solid rock that experts say no bomb can break through. Trump said America is watching it and warned Iran not to 'get cute' - but since nobody has a weapon that can reach it, the threat is really a way to scare Iran and push oil prices around, not a plan to actually blow it up.

Fighters called the Houthis kept moving along Yemen's coast and started attacking nearby islands, getting closer to a narrow sea gate that about a tenth of the world's ships pass through. What is new is that Iran is reportedly helping them with officers and weapons - which means Iran gets a second place to squeeze world shipping without risking its own soldiers.

American wholesale prices rose 5.4 per cent over the year, but almost all of the jump was fuel: diesel alone went up 24 per cent in one month. That matters because a central bank can slow down shopping by making borrowing expensive, but it cannot make more fuel. So raising rates now may just make people poorer without fixing the actual problem.

The Supreme Court blocked Missouri from using a new map of voting districts that Republicans drew to win an extra seat in Congress. Ordinary Missourians had collected hundreds of thousands of signatures to force a public vote on it first. The same week, Trump promised every American adult $5,000 if Republicans win - two different ways of trying to move a majority that is only five seats wide.

The leader of Ethiopia's Tigray region said his side has signed a permanent agreement with rebel groups from other corners of the country, but refused to say who they are. If it is real, Ethiopia's government would have to fight in three places at once. If it is a bluff, it is a way to get a better deal in talks - and refusing to name names is the clue that it might be the second one.

risk.line: HIGH, held for the fourth consecutive pass, and the discipline of holding it matters more today than on any day this week because the board acquired a THIRD escalation vector in a single afternoon and the CRITICAL gate still went untouched. That gate is written in bodies and hulls - a struck US-flagged merchant hull or a confirmed American death - and it survived the Muwaffaq Salti strike on American aircraft in Jordan, it survived the IRGC taking an Anduril underwater vehicle at the mouth of Hormuz, and nothing today reached it either. What changed is the shape of the risk rather than its level. First, the Houthis converted Mocha into position: Ansar Allah pressed Dhubab and began attacking the Hanish islands, and France 24 reports Revolutionary Guards gave direct guidance to the coastal advance with Tehran promising more funding, weapons and senior officers to escalate against Saudi Arabia - which reframes a Yemeni land war as an Iranian second front bought cheap. Second, the tanker exchange became mutual: US missiles hit five Iranian tankers near Kharg Island and Jask, Iran struck ships near the Strait of Hormuz, and Hormuz transits fell to seven on Wednesday against a ten-day average of fourteen. Third, and newest, Trump put the deepest target in Iran on the table by name, advising Tehran 'not to get cute because we will have to hit them very hard' over activity at Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La - the tunnel complex two kilometres from Natanz that CSIS, reading 9 July Airbus and 9 August Satellogic imagery, says has seen more road activity in 2026 than at any point in its history. The price board answered through the middle of the economy rather than its edges: Brent at $105.26 and touching $106, WTI at $100.04, wholesale prices up 5.4 per cent on the year with diesel alone up 24.1 per cent in a month, the national diesel average at a record $5.98, and futures moving from 61 to roughly 70 per cent odds that the Federal Reserve hikes on Wednesday - six days after the ECB already did, on staff projections whose data cut-off predates all of this. Two chokepoints, one named nuclear target, two central banks tightening into the shock, and Hormuz at day 194 of closure by insurance rather than by mines. The board has never been wider. The gate is still, precisely, unmet.

forecasts.q: Brent stays inside the $80-100 band
forecasts.note: CUT 8, the largest cut this book has made, and it is a mechanical barrier recompute rather than a narrative move - the same method as yesterday's cut, applied to a price that moved 1.8 per cent closer to the wall. Brent traded $99.16 and touched $99.22, the highest since 24 July, on the Houthi strikes. The geometry, with the inputs published per the 09-06 anchor rule: log distance to the $100 barrier 0.0084, roughly eleven sessions left, realised volatility annualising near 60 per cent for a daily sigma of 3.78 per cent, so the barrier sits 0.22 sigma away. Continuous first-passage gives 5 per cent survival; the Broadie-Glasserman continuity correction for DISCRETE monitoring, which this question needs because it resolves on daily CLOSES rather than intraday prints, shifts the effective barrier by 0.58 sigma and lifts survival to about 19 per cent. Anchor recomputed 28 to 19. The mark sits two points below the anchor on the same named drift term as yesterday: OPEC+ has removed its capping mechanism and most remaining spare capacity sits behind a contested strait. Note honestly that a $100 print in a search result today came from a 23 July article, not from Tuesday's tape - the live number is $99, and the two-point gap matters at this distance.

forecasts.q: US diesel crack spread settles back below $45/bbl before 15 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: CUT 3, and the reason this is NOT the double-count refused yesterday is worth stating precisely. Yesterday's held evidence was the bunker squeeze - a downstream consequence of the same crude-conversion constraint already priced. Today's evidence is a different category: physical damage to conversion capacity itself. Aramco's Jazan complex, 400,000 barrels a day and roughly a tenth of the company's net refining capacity, was reported hit by the Financial Times, in a plant already shut twice since late July and restarted late on 30 August. A refinery that keeps being knocked over is a supply event, not a spread consequence. The crack falls when conversion capacity returns; every strike on Jazan pushes that date right. Held to 3 points because Reuters could not immediately verify the Jazan hit and the Saudi energy ministry has confirmed only that operations at some facilities halted.

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire holds 30+ days
forecasts.note: CUT 2 after two sessions of deliberate holds, and the dated falsifier published on 09-06 has now RUN. It said the capitals pause would be informative if it lapsed with no extension and no jointly acknowledged text. It lapsed exactly on schedule and Russia put 166 drones, 32 cruise missiles and ballistic and anti-ship rounds into Ukraine within hours, killing five and wounding 63. A truce whose duration matches an envoy's itinerary to the hour is a scheduling accommodation, not a de-escalation - and it demonstrates that Moscow can switch the air campaign on and off at will, which is evidence of confidence rather than exhaustion. Fortna's condition is used a third time and now in the direction that costs us: no monitors, no guarantor, no demarcation, and now a scored falsifier. Only 2 points because Zelenskyy simultaneously said talks are possible this month, and a party that expects to meet is not a party that has walked.

forecasts.q: US-China tariff truce collapses before Nov expiry
forecasts.note: CUT 2, and the discipline is separating the new fact from the loud one. The loud fact is a record surplus: exports up 25 per cent, the August surplus $119.1bn against $112.5bn in July, $805.5bn year to date, shipments to the US up 34.4 per cent. That is a KNOWN structural condition - China ran $1.2tn last year - and known conditions do not move probabilities. The new fact is that both governments are exploring reciprocal tariff cuts on $30bn of goods each side, which is the first numbered de-escalation the file has produced since the May truce, sixteen days before a state visit. Composition reinforces it: the surge is in semiconductors, computing hardware and AI-adjacent goods, meaning American demand is pulling the flow. A country importing what it needs is a country that renews.

forecasts.q: Saudi Arabia publicly moves toward enrichment or the bomb
forecasts.note: RAISED 2, the smaller of today's two raises, on a demonstrated air-defence shortfall rather than on any nuclear signal. Drones and ballistic missiles reached a coalition airbase at Khamis Mushait and Aramco sites at Abha, Najran and Jazan, wounding 73, on top of direct Iranian strikes on Ras Tanura and Prince Sultan Air Base between February and June. Sagan's security model is the framework: proliferation pressure rises when a state's protector visibly cannot cover it, and Riyadh's revealed strategy through this entire war has been to convert insecurity into a HIGHER PRICE for the American guarantee rather than into an independent programme. That is why this is +2 and not +6 - what today buys is leverage in a guarantee negotiation, and only the failure of that negotiation would buy a programme.

forecasts.q: Xi state visit to US happens in September
forecasts.note: RAISED 1 to the anchor, and a one-point move is all an expected event confirming on schedule is worth. Sixteen days out, with reporting now describing a concrete pre-summit deliverable under negotiation - reciprocal tariff cuts on $30bn of goods each way - rather than only logistics. A summit with a numbered agenda item is marginally harder to cancel than a summit with a guest list.

forecasts.q: Major US/Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes
forecasts.note: HELD, and this is today's most important non-move. Iranian-aligned forces struck four Saudi cities and halted operations at energy facilities; the intuitive read is that an attack on a US ally's oil raises the odds of American strikes on Iran. The base rate says the opposite, and it is the single most relevant analog available: Abqaiq, 14 September 2019, took 5.7 million barrels a day off line - half of Saudi output, the most damaging attack ever on oil infrastructure - was attributed by Washington to Iran directly, and produced NO American strike on Iran. What it produced was a troop deployment and a sanctions round. Damage to Saudi assets has never been the trigger; damage to American ones has. The 09-06 resolution-criteria pin is restated verbatim and still binds: multi-day, state targets inside Iran.

forecasts.q: Hormuz transits recover past 50% of pre-war volume
forecasts.note: HELD for a third session, and the refusal is the same one, applied to genuinely better evidence. Qatar's foreign ministry said reopening the strait UNCONDITIONALLY is a top priority - a harder word than yesterday's formulation - and the Qatari prime minister raised it with Wang Yi in BEIJING, which is a new venue and the correct one, since China is the party that actually prices Iranian compliance by buying the oil. But this question resolves on a volume print and an appeal is not a transit. Logged as the strongest diplomatic input this file has had in a fortnight, and still not a number.

forecasts.note: HELD. Qatar asking for UNCONDITIONAL reopening is, read carefully, evidence on the other side of this question - an unconditional reopening is precisely one that preserves no administrative machinery. But Qatar's ask is not a deal term, and this question resolves on what an agreement CONTAINS, not on what a third party requests. Ostovar's mechanism is unchanged: the Guard converts each crisis into an institution that outlives it.

Brent at $99 is an inflation input and the ten-year at 4.77 is above this board's red line, but neither is a US data release and the Fed does not act on the barrel directly - it acts on what the barrel does to expectations, which prints later. Eight days to the meeting. The two-sided resolution leg is armed and unchanged.

Street mobilisation against the AfD is precisely the variable that failed in Saxony-Anhalt, where turnout rose from about 60 to about 80 per cent and the AfD still gained; so it is logged as evidence with no directional signal until the 20 September result.

forecasts.note: HELD. Nothing today touched Beijing's Iranian purchases. Qatar lobbying Wang Yi on the strait is an approach to China as a mediator, which is a different transaction from China cutting its own barrels. Drezner: intensity is not compliance.

forecasts.note: HELD. A 166-drone night is an air-campaign event, not a line-of-contact one, and this question resolves on ground taken. Autumn mud then winter depress mechanised advance in the historical series; the counter-argument is that a Russia demonstrating it controls the tempo may be husbanding for a winter push.

forecasts.note: HELD, and today strengthened it without justifying a move, because it is already high. A pause that exists only as an unwritten understanding covering a visit, which lapses on a clock with no text on either side, is the exact ancestor of the Korean 1953 shape this question describes.
